title: Zoning-law library, second pass (documents only): for each remaining development option (2-3, 5, 6-7, 8, 9, 10, 11) the Zoning Resolution sections that decide it, read from the official text, with what the program handles, what it does not, and what stays not sure
objective: Write a documents-only second pass of the zoning-law library under docs/zoning-law-library/options/ (extends planned milestone M3; builds no code, no rule, no capture): one file per option family - options 2-3 (qualifying affordable and senior housing, the Universal Affordability Preference), 5 (ground-floor shops with residences above: overlay use permission, overlay floor area, mixed-building floor area, height and street wall), 6-7 (community facility: floor area, coverage, height, setback, yards, the mixed-building combination), 8 (split lot: the two readings of options-sections.md kept apart - two buildings on one zoning lot, and a zoning lot divided by a district boundary - and what the owner's sample shows, by pointer only), 9 (shared housing: use, density, standards), 10 (parking and the transit zones, plus one parking / loading / bicycle-parking applicability line for every option, DB-180), 11 (which add-ons may be combined and the combination ceilings). Each file gives, per Zoning Resolution section: section id, title, official URL, the last-amended date the official page shows, capture state (the snapshot file in docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/ or NOT CAPTURED), handled state (the rule file under services/api/app/rules/rulesets/ or NOT HANDLED); then a reading that states the applicable rule, the definitions it relies on, exceptions, overlay and special-district effects, the measurement basis, the zoning-lot scope, the facts about a lot the program would need and where each could come from, and every point that is not sure with its next step. options-sections.md gains, per option, a pointer to its file and an updated state for each item it marks NOT CAPTURED or not sure (resolved with a cited official source, or restated as open). research-log.md records every search. Every file carries the unreviewed-draft label (ADR-007); nothing is Verified; no option is called compliant, buildable, feasible or preferred; no eligibility is decided; no figure for the benchmark lot is computed.
business_reason: All eleven options stay in scope (owner, D-090 R248-R265; D-094 source-002) but the master plan marks options 2-11 not planned because the law each still lacks has not been read. The first pass (M3-T006) listed what each option needs and left sections NOT CAPTURED or not sure (23-154, the community-facility envelope, the shared-housing sections, the meaning of split lot). The owner asked for research helpers on the remaining options' rules (D-094 R104) and approved ten helpers tonight (R119). This pass turns the list into readings a rules task can be contracted from.

acceptance_scenarios.given: every Zoning Resolution section an option file relies on
acceptance_scenarios.then: the section has its id, title, official URL, the last-amended date shown on the official page, a capture state that matches docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/ (the snapshot file, or NOT CAPTURED), and a handled state that names the exact rule file or NOT HANDLED

it states the applicable rule, the definitions relied on, exceptions, overlay and special-district effects, the measurement basis, the zoning-lot scope and the lot facts the program would need with a possible source for each; every point the producer is not sure of says not sure with its next step

acceptance_scenarios.given: each item options-sections.md marks NOT CAPTURED or not sure for options 2 to 11
acceptance_scenarios.when: options-sections.md and the option's file are read
acceptance_scenarios.then: the item is resolved with a cited official source read for this pass, or restated as still open with the exact missing item and its next step; none is silently dropped

the two readings (two buildings on one zoning lot; a zoning lot divided by a district boundary) are kept apart, each with its sections; what the owner's sample shows is given by pointer only (page number, no copied text); the question which reading the owner intends stays open unless the owner has answered it

it has one parking, loading and bicycle-parking applicability line per option naming the sections that decide it, with the transit-zone membership of the benchmark lot stated as a recorded value with its source, or as not known with the search made

acceptance_scenarios.given: every search the pass rests on
acceptance_scenarios.then: each has the source, the query or URL, found / not found / access blocked, the missing item and the next step; an access block is recorded, never evaded

it touches only the allowed paths; no file quotes more than one short passage per cited item; no third-party document is copied; no code, rule, capture, evidence record or review-register file changes

acceptance_scenarios.when: it is searched for status words
acceptance_scenarios.then: each carries the unreviewed-draft label; nothing is labelled Verified; no option is called compliant, buildable, feasible, optimal or preferred; no eligibility (affordable, senior, shared housing) is decided; no floor area, height, unit count or parking count is computed for the benchmark lot

risks: zoningresolution.planning.nyc.gov pages can time out or refuse non-browser fetches (23-154 returned HTTP 403 in the first pass): use the documented print/PDF channel, record a block with the URL, never evade.
The 2024 City of Yes amendments renumbered sections: every section number is taken from the official page read for this pass, never from memory or from an older document.
Readings of eligibility programs are legal determinations the program does not make: state the conditions, decide nothing.
Public repository: pointers and at most one short quote per item; the competitor's sample is cited by page number only.
A reading here changes no result, rule or label; a later rules task works its own independent example before any result changes (D-093).
path_notes: Lane L (library), disjoint from the report lane: a new folder docs/zoning-law-library/options/ plus options-sections.md, owned by no other task in flight; docs/** is covered by Lane C's ownership rule (no OWNERSHIP.yaml change). Research helper returns are saved in the session folder outside git and cited in options/research-log.md.

progress_log.message: claimed; read-only research helpers dispatched first
